identityReadiness.schema: 0001 defines principals principal_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, status, nullable display_name, created_at, updated_at; principal_password_credentials principal_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, email_normalized TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, password_hash, created_at, updated_at. No credential foreign key exists in this migration: do not invent one. 0002 defines the independent principal/Sesh mapping table and creator unique index; ZB does not use it, but complete migration history must be reconciled.
identityReadiness.persistence: One D1 batch inserts principal and credential and reads their joined exact identity. Requires success on all three results and changes 1/1/0, exact metadata/readback and transactional rollback on unique conflict. Remote compatibility remains unverified.

identityReadiness.checks: Under separate read-only approval, verify whoami account against owner-approved target, info database UUID against committed ID, applied migration names against both files, no unexpected pending migrations, exact column/null/PK/unique constraints and unique-index columns via PRAGMA index_info for returned index names. Missing migration-history table or disagreement stops activation; do not repair/migrate in a read-only slice.
identityReadiness.ownerRaceGate: Immediately before signup, separately repeat exact normalized-email credential count and joined principal lookup for the owner-selected email. Expected zero before registration. If any account appears, do not register again; verify existing identity through the canonical login/owner process. Prior reports of absence are not current remote proof.

trustedOrigin.derivation: astro.config.mjs site supplies import.meta.env.SITE. C1 validates root HTTPS URL in production and passes new URL(site).origin to A. A requires exact Origin equality; absent/null/alternate origins fail. Canonical SITE, adapter/build settings and existing sitemap exclusions remain unchanged.

trustedIngress.evidenceLimit: Cloudflare Astro adapter, cloudflare:workers env and Wrangler Worker name indicate intended Workers architecture. Repository files do not prove deployed DNS, routes, account, proxy configuration or absence of alternate origins.
laterReadOnlyChecklist: Verify canonical zone/account, DNS records and proxy status in trusted Cloudflare dashboard/API; TLS and canonical domain route must terminate at the intended Worker.
Verify active Worker deployment/version, custom domain/routes, effective bindings and canonical path ownership; verify workers.dev and preview URL exposure policies explicitly.

Inventory any external origin/load balancer/tunnel and alternate domains; prove an origin cannot accept a caller-supplied CF-Connecting-IP and forward it as trusted identity. No external origin is established by repository evidence.
Review same-zone Worker subrequests and header rewrite rules: platform-controlled ingress alone must not silently authorize attacker-controlled header forwarding.

With registration disabled, inspect canonical endpoint headers/status and infrastructure metadata without credential bodies. Obtain platform configuration evidence that external supplied CF-Connecting-IP is overwritten/controlled; do not treat a 503 or CF-Ray alone as proof.
Confirm missing/noncanonical IP remains fail closed; activation switch asserts separately verified provenance rather than verifying it itself.

limiterConfiguration.evidence: Installed config-schema.json ratelimits items require name:string, namespace_id:string, simple:{limit:number,period:10|60}, no extra properties. Installed validateRateLimitBinding agrees. Thus 5/60 and 30/60 are expressible; no threshold contract correction needed.
limiterConfiguration.templateOnly: Not an executable approved patch: namespace placeholders must be replaced by separately reviewed distinct account-scoped namespace identifiers after collision/resource checks. No identifiers allocated here. Merge keys into existing configuration rather than replacing unrelated vars/bindings. Installed schema proves shape/period, not live namespace validity or account entitlement. Named environments, if later introduced, need explicit ratelimits declarations because they are not inherited.
limiterConfiguration.types: After approved declarations, separately regenerate with npx wrangler types --config=wrangler.jsonc and inspect generated diff; never hand-edit worker-configuration.d.ts. Expect limiter bindings and switch representation; root current generated Env lacks all three. Existing C1 safely uses unknown structural acquisition and builds without these types.
limiterConfiguration.semantics: IP limiter runs before shared limiter; shared uses registration:shared within each location. Counters are not a globally consistent quota. Local two-slot protection is per isolate, not fleet-wide. Strict Origin does not prevent automated clients supplying it; HIBP screens passwords, not humans. These controls are proportionate candidates for a bounded initial window, conditional on owner acceptance of residual distributed-abuse risk and verified capacity. They do not establish safety for indefinite open signup.

activation.representation: Nonsecret ordinary Cloudflare Worker var, preferably repository-reviewed vars string false for disabled-first deployment. Only exact string true enables. Missing also disables; never boolean true or a secret for this nonsecret flag.
activation.separation: Limiter declaration and regenerated typing may share a reviewed configuration slice while switch stays false/absent. Changing it to true is a separate explicit activation slice and deployment/version review. Committing configuration alone does not update live env.
activation.lifecycle: UNRESOLVED OWNER PRODUCT DECISION: temporary controlled owner-registration window versus continued public registration. Recommend proposing a temporary window, but do not silently adopt it. Temporary policy requires explicit later disablement/deployment; continued public policy accepts ongoing abuse, capacity and external dependency exposure.
activation.disablement: Set exact string false in the authoritative configuration source and deploy the reviewed disabled version under approval, or use a separately approved supported live configuration rollout with repository reconciliation. Verify new requests yield fixed 503 before body/security/database calls. Disabling does not cancel already in-flight operations, erase accounts or invalidate existing login sessions.

pwnedPasswords.implementation: Complete injected adapter; production route injects ordinary runtime fetch and crypto.subtle. No additional outbound binding appears required by source; network policy/reachability still needs live verification.
pwnedPasswords.disclosure: GET sends only five uppercase SHA-1 prefix characters derived server-side, Add-Padding:true, credentials:omit, redirect:error, cache:no-store. No plaintext, full hash, suffix or account email is sent by implementation. Service still observes server network/request metadata; partial hash disclosure is not zero disclosure. SHA-1 is range lookup only; stored credentials use Argon2id.
pwnedPasswords.approval: LIVE USE NOT APPROVED. Separate owner privacy/external-service approval required before any real request or enabled signup.
pwnedPasswords.laterSafeVerification: After explicit approval, request one documented synthetic five-character range from the intended deployed runtime through an approved isolated diagnostic, no real password/email, no identity write; verify HTTPS success, redirect rejection, streamed bounds, padding-compatible grammar and timeout behavior. Do not add a public diagnostic endpoint. Ordinary local network success would not prove deployed-runtime access.

capacity.requestBody: 8192 streamed bytes; canonical declared Content-Length checked; 5000ms body deadline; flat exact email/password JSON, malformed UTF-8/duplicates rejected.
capacity.hibp: 3000ms total checker deadline including digest/fetch/read; 1048576 response bytes; at most 25000 lines; 35-character uppercase suffix and 1-20 digit counts; malformed/uncertain results unavailable.
capacity.password: 15-128 Unicode scalars, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes; original password unchanged.
capacity.hash: Argon2id v19, memory 19456KiB, iterations2, parallelism1, salt16bytes, output32bytes; JavaScript noble implementation performs synchronous derivation inside async methods.
capacity.concurrency: Two registration slots per isolate, immediate rejection without queue; release once. Not a global concurrency limit and not a login concurrency limiter.
capacity.remainingChecks: Verify intended Workers plan CPU/wall-time/memory/subrequest limits and Argon2 behavior under actual runtime, two simultaneous jobs plus session/login workload, outbound latency, limiter behavior, D1 batch compatibility and neutral-response timing. Use separately approved isolated deployed performance harness with synthetic data, not production identity writes. Existing unit tests and local workerd do not prove plan capacity. Do not claim a total registration deadline: hashing/database work has no additional overall deadline in source.

sessionReadiness.evidence: astro.config.mjs has no explicit session driver. Installed @astrojs/cloudflare enables default Cloudflare KV session driver and generated deployment configuration represents SESSION. Root Wrangler/generated root Env alone does not demonstrate its deployed persistence.
sessionReadiness.gate: Verify effective generated config, SESSION resource/environment isolation, deployed driver, cookie secure/HttpOnly/SameSite/path/expiry behavior, async Astro get compatibility and login persistence across requests. Missing runtime session infrastructure may make login unavailable despite successful registration. No new session configuration or provisioning authorized here.

deployment.evidence: package.json build runs astro build then search:index; deploy runs wrangler deploy; publish combines them. release also runs lint/typecheck and verify:production; existing PowerShell verification checks general public endpoints, not registration-specific readiness. CI validates main pull requests/pushes with npm run check; it is not an automatic production deployment workflow.
deployment.preflight: Explicit account/Worker target approval; inspect .wrangler/deploy/config.json redirect and generated dist/server/wrangler.json after build, effective SESSION and other bindings, disabled activation and artifact version. No deployment command ran here. Do not blindly use release as a harmless check because it deploys.
deployment.postflight: Verify exact deployed version/custom-domain association; register/login headers/rendering, disabled registration 503/no writes or outbound checks, sitemap exclusions, ingress and session resources. Public endpoint verification alone does not prove all bindings/schema.

browserMatrix: Before activation: deployed /register and /login render, labels/focus/keyboard/status region work, no analytics/third-party resources, expected CSP console/network behavior and no secret-bearing telemetry.

JS disabled and intentional script failure: disabled unnamed fields prevent credential native fallback/GET; no credentials in query/fragment/navigation, autocomplete/new-password/current-password and password-manager behavior verified with synthetic values.

Disabled registration: synthetic valid-looking submission receives fixed503, exact same-origin POST JSON, credentials:same-origin/redirect:error/no-store, password cleared, no duplicate pending submission; prove server disabled before submitting.

Intercept synthetic responses locally or through approved browser interception to verify202/error/uncertain UX without enabling registration or writing accounts; do not treat intercepted202 as real persistence proof.

No production test identity required merely to test render/fallback/fetch/feedback. Successful real login cookie/session cannot be proved without an account: defer to owner login after registration or separately approve an existing test-safe identity path, never create one automatically.

After separate activation/owner registration: owner verifies normal login on canonical origin, session cookie attributes and subsequent authenticated session behavior without revealing password to agent; no FOOD entitlement or redirect implied.

ownerProcedure.preconditions: All approved configuration/schema/ingress/privacy/capacity/deployment/browser gates passed, activation policy selected and explicitly enabled; repeat exact-email absence gate immediately before signup.
ownerProcedure.steps: Owner opens https://theriverkeptflowing.com/register, enters riveryoung100@gmail.com and owner-selected password directly in deployed browser, submits once, treats neutral acknowledgement as processing rather than proof of account creation, proceeds to /login and authenticates normally. Uncertain registration: try normal sign-in before retrying; no automatic retry. Existing account gate stops new registration.
ownerProcedure.passwordBoundary: Real password only entered by owner in deployed browser; never supplied to Codex/ChatGPT, Git, shell/history, logs, config or screenshots shared with agent.

postRegistration.readOnlyQueryTemplate: SELECT c.principal_id,p.status FROM principal_password_credentials c LEFT JOIN principals p ON p.principal_id=c.principal_id WHERE c.email_normalized='<OWNER_APPROVED_EXACT_NORMALIZED_EMAIL>';
postRegistration.verification: Under separate narrow identity-read approval, exact normalized owner email yields exactly one credential joined to exactly one active canonical principal; parsePrincipalId accepts unchanged ID. Inspect counts and orphan/mismatch conditions without selecting password_hash. Unique email/PK constraints plus atomic registration prevent duplicates in supported schema; do not infer historical unrelated principal ownership from email alone. Owner confirms canonical login/session corresponds to same ID. Any missing/inactive/mismatch/uncertainty stops handoff, no manual repair or guessed principal.
postRegistration.privacy: Restrict identifying output to protected review, not generic production config or new public endpoints. Email in this procedural specification is owner intent, not an injected configuration value.

foodHandoff: After verified canonical active principal, separate explicit owner approval configures RIVER_FOOD_ADMIN_PRINCIPAL_ID via per-environment Cloudflare secret/protected configuration per FOOD-002Y. Principal ID is identifying privileged configuration, not a bearer credential; possession alone grants nothing. Never infer/default/manufacture it or put owner email into generic vars. Registration/login confers no FOOD permission. No FOOD admin configuration here.
rollback: Prefer disable switch and verify fixed503, then review approved Worker version rollback if required. Preserve accounts and schema; no reset/rebase/delete/database rollback. Disabling registration preserves login and existing identities; consider in-flight uncertainty before retry. Fail closed on missing dependencies/external failures. Keep audit evidence of approved versions/configuration without secrets or passwords.
